title: leah-wong-private-deploy-networking-incident-notes
content:
Quick notes / breadcrumbs - Private deploy networking incident (VPC peering + DNS + TLS + egress)
Owner: Leah Wong
Collaborators: Noah Gomez, Samir Patel
Dates: initial detection 2026-02-19 17:12 UTC, ongoing debugging notes below (timestamps local).

Summary:
- Customer on private deployment reported intermittent 504s and TLS handshake failures when calling Redwood control-plane endpoints from their VPC. A subset of pods in the private deployment cannot reach external key management and remote model artifact storage.
- Suspected areas: VPC peering route tables, DNS resolution for control-plane hostnames (split-horizon / private hosted zone), TLS termination mismatch, and egress/NAT issues.

Observed symptoms:
- App logs show repeated: "TLS handshake error: EOF" and "x509: certificate signed by unknown authority" for calls to s3-compatible artifact store and control-plane API.
- Some requests return 504 with upstream timeout in the nginx sidecar around 2026-02-19 17:05-17:20 UTC.
- From customer VPC we sometimes get NXDOMAIN for control-plane.mycompany.internal but public name resolves fine.
- Intermittent traceroute shows asymmetric path: packets to CP hop through VPC-peering route then disappears at peer VPC router.

Commands tried (raw outputs truncated / notes):
- dig +trace control-plane.mycompany.internal @10.0.0.2
  -> sometimes returns NXDOMAIN, sometimes returns private IP (10.20.4.5)
- nslookup control-plane.mycompany.internal 10.0.0.2
  -> server can't find control-plane.mycompany.internal: NXDOMAIN (when failing)
- kubectl exec -it pod/ingress-abc -- curl -v https://control-plane.mycompany.internal/health
  * Connected to 10.20.4.5 (10.20.4.5) port 443 (#0)
  * TLS handshake: SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure
  * Closing connection 0
  curl: (35) SSL handshake failed
- openssl s_client -connect control-plane.mycompany.internal:443 -servername control-plane.mycompany.internal
  CONNECTED(00000003)
  140735123456000:error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca:
  ---
  certificate subject= /CN=control-plane.mycompany.internal
  issuer= /CN=internal-root-ca
  ---
- tcpdump -ni eth0 host 10.20.4.5 and port 443
  -> TCP SYNs seen, SYN-ACK from 10.20.4.5, then RST occasionally.
- traceroute -n 10.20.4.5
  -> 10.0.0.1 10.0.1.1 10.20.0.1 * *
  stops at peer router sometimes.
- iptables -S (on node)
  -> no user rules blocking outbound 443; default ACCEPT.
- aws ec2 describe-vpc-peering-connections --filters "Name=requester-vpc-info.vpc-id,Values=vpc-aaa"
  -> status: active, AccepterOwnerId matches peer account, accepter-allow? (need to check).
- aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters "Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-aaa"
  -> route to 10.20.0.0/16 via pcx-1234 present in rtb-0a1b2c.
- aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters "Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-bbb" (peer)
  -> route to 10.0.0.0/16 via pcx-1234 present, but one private RT has missing route (rtb-0d3e4f) -> possible culprit.

Error snippets copied from logs:
- "x509: certificate signed by unknown authority (control-plane.mycompany.internal:443)"
- "TLS handshake error: EOF"
- "504 upstream read timeout from 10.20.4.5"
- "dial tcp 10.20.4.5:443: connect: connection refused" (rare)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Split-horizon DNS + caching causing some nodes to resolve public IP while others resolve private IP; wide TTL mismatch leading to connecting to incompatible endpoints (public cert vs internal CA).
   - Evidence: NXDOMAIN intermittency, differing dig outputs, cert issuer = internal-root-ca (internal-only), some pods see public name with public IP and get CA mismatch.
2) VPC peering route tables inconsistent across subnets/route tables in the peer VPC. A specific RT associated with worker subnet in peer VPC missing route back to requester VPC causing asymmetric routing -> some flows drop.
   - Evidence: describe-route-tables shows one RT missing the peering route. traceroute drops at peer router.
3) Intermittent egress/NAT gateway exhaustion in the customer VPC causing outgoing TLS connections to be SNAT'd unpredictably and lead to connection reset/timeouts.
   - Evidence: 504s align with high throughput periods; need NAT metrics.
4) TLS cert trust chain not installed on some nodes (internal CA missing from system trust store) -> x509 unknown authority.
   - Evidence: openssl indicates issuer internal-root-ca. But why only some pods? Maybe different base images or sidecar not configured to mount CA bundle.
5) Security group or NACL rules on peer VPC intermittently blocking traffic (less likely because SYN-ACK seen).

Immediate remediation attempts (actions & outcomes):
- Added missing route to rtb-0d3e4f (peer VPC) -> preliminary improvement: traceroute completed from one test node. Customer reported fewer 504s in next 20 min.
- Pushed CA bundle to problematic daemonset (sidecar) on nodes that were failing -> decreased x509 errors locally. Need wider rollout.
- Increased NAT gateway capacity / rotated to standby NAT -> need to monitor egress metrics (CloudWatch) for drop in SNAT errors.

Diagnostic TODOs (next steps):
- Run distributed DNS check across all worker subnets and nodes (script) to capture which resolver returns what for control-plane.mycompany.internal and TTLs. Collect /var/lib/containers/resolv.conf variations.
- Check kubelet/node image variants and sidecar container mounts to confirm CA bundle presence. CI recently rolled a new sidecar image 2026-02-18; correlate.
- Confirm all route tables in peer VPC have routes for requester's CIDR. Use AWS API to enumerate rtb associations vs subnets and list missing pcx entries.
- Gather NAT gateway CloudWatch metrics (ActiveConnections, BytesOut, ConnectionErrors) for timeframe 2026-02-19 16:30-18:00 UTC.
- Add per-pod tcpdump + packet capture for a failing pod during reproduce window and share pcaps.
- Add more verbose nginx sidecar logging for upstream connect timeouts (enable debug for 10-15 min window).

Notes to self / hypotheses to test in code:
- If split-horizon DNS is the cause, forcing kube-dns / CoreDNS config to prioritize the private hosted zone for the specific domain should reduce misresolution. But must verify there are no override records in the peer account.
- If CA bundle missing: extend the DaemonSet to mount /etc/ssl/certs/custom-internal-ca.pem into the app sidecar and restart pods in waves. Prefer image-based fix for long-term.

Repro steps (minimal):
1) From worker subnet A (vpc-aaa), get dig @10.0.0.2 control-plane.mycompany.internal (repeat 10x)
2) curl -v https://control-plane.mycompany.internal/health and capture TLS handshake output
3) traceroute -n to the IP returned, note hop where route drops
4) On peer side, run aws ec2 describe-route-tables filtered by associated subnet id to ensure pcx present

Slack notes: pinged #private-deploy-debug at 2026-02-19T18:05Z with initial findings. Noah to check route table associations in peer account, Samir to push the CA bundle to remaining nodes.

Open questions / things I forgot to check:
- Are there any VPC endpoint services in the peer account with policy that might rate-limit TLS handshakes?
- Is there any intermediate proxy (transparent) in the path that rewrites SNI? (Check ALB vs NLB configs)
- Confirm if control-plane cert is rotated recently (ask platform-cert team).

Anchor files / artifacts to attach when filing postmortem:
- pcap captures: pcap-controlplane-failing-20260219.pcap (stored in /tmp on my laptop)
- aws describe-route-tables outputs (rtb-list-20260219.json)
- dig/nslookup logs (dns-checks-20260219.log)
- nginx sidecar logs (nginx-debug-20260219.log)

Quick decision log:
- 2026-02-19 19:10 UTC: added missing peering route in rtb-0d3e4f (rolling change) -> partial recovery observed.
- 2026-02-19 20:05 UTC: deployed CA bundle to daemonset on 3 failing nodes -> x509 errors reduced.

Will follow up with a short writeup once we confirm stable for 24 hours. If symptoms return, escalate to platform networking and request packet captures from the peer account's router.

-- Leah
